governing_table.edition: 8th Edition (2023), in force until 2026-12-30; the 9th Edition (2026) takes effect 2026-12-31
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (repeated as Table [P] 2902.1 in the Florida Building Code, Building, Chapter 29)
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 403.1, based on the actual use of the building or space. Uses not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by the Florida Building Code, Building.

building_code_duplicate.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space.
building_code_duplicate.points_to_plumbing_code_quote: The provisions of this chapter and the Florida Building Code, Plumbing shall govern the erection, installation, alteration, repairs, relocation, replacement, addition to, use or maintenance of plumbing equipment and systems.
building_code_duplicate.note: The Building table is marked [P] (maintained by the plumbing code) and carries the same ratios in the three rows read here. The Business row was compared cell by cell; the Restaurant and Educational rows were compared as text. Florida's potty-parity section (403.1.3) appears in the Plumbing volume only; the Building chapter's 2902.1.3 is 'Lavatory Distribution'.

city_adoption.quote: Effective December 31, 2023, the applicable codes in the State of Florida are: ... Florida Building Code- Plumbing / 8th Edition (2023)

governing_table.read_on: UpCodes (secondary). The official ICC viewer (codes.iccsafe.org/content/FLPC2023P1 and FLBC2023P1) returned a captcha page / HTTP 403 to automated access.

amendments.text: No City of Miami amendment to the fixture table was found: the city's Building Department page lists the state code editions and has no sentence about local amendments. The table read is already Florida's own version of the 2021 International Plumbing Code table; the Florida-specific additions that matter are Section 403.1.3 (potty parity for assembly occupancies, from s. 553.86, Florida Statutes), Section 403.1.4 (outdoor areas count), Section 403.2.2 (separate restrooms by sex for covered entities under s. 553.865) and, for public schools, Section 453.16 of the Building volume.
amendments.quote: codes and regulations established by the State of Florida and Miami-Dade County.

state_additions.quote: In assembly occupancies, restrooms which are open to the public must have a ratio of 3:2 water closets provided for women as the combined total of water closets and urinals provided for men, unless these are two or fewer such fixtures for men, in accordance with §553.86, Florida Statutes. The ratio established by potty parity is not required to be maintained for the additional fixtures provided in excess of the minimum required fixtures.
state_additions.exception_quote: Exception: This section does not apply to establishments licensed under Chapter 509, Florida Statutes, if the establishment does not provide meeting or banquet rooms which accommodate more than 150 people, and the establishment has at least the same number of water closets for women as the combined total of water closets and urinals for men.
state_additions.definition_quote: New construction. Means new construction, building, alteration, rehabilitation or repair that equals or exceeds 50 percent of the replacement value existing on October 1, 1992, unless the same was under design or construction, or under construction contract before October 1, 1992.

state_additions.quote: For the purposes of calculating the minimum number of required plumbing facilities, the requirements of Table 403.1 shall apply to any areas outside of the building that are used as part of the building's designated occupancy (single or mixed).
Covered entities, as defined in §553.865, Florida Statutes, shall provide separate restrooms and changing facilities based on biological sex, or to provide single-user unisex facilities.

Educational and ancillary facilities shall be provided with toilets, hand washing facilities, and drinking fountains for all occupants, in ratios and accessible as required by the Florida Building Code, Florida law, and federal requirements.

office.row_label: 2 | Business | Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: No urinal column; the header says 'WATER CLOSETS (URINALS: SEE SECTION 424.2)'. Urinals are optional substitutes for up to 50 percent of the required water closets.
office.lavatories: 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 (one cell spanning male and female)
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink
office.note: The water-closet cell spans the male and female columns, so the ratio applies to each sex's half of the occupant load. Remaining cells: bathtubs/showers none, drinking fountain 1 per 100, 1 service sink (not required at 15 or fewer occupants, footnote e).

restaurant.row_label: 1 | Assembly | Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: No urinal column; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly occupancies.
restaurant.lavatories: 1 per 200 (one cell spanning male and female)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 | — | 1 per 500 | 1 service sink
restaurant.footnote_d_quote: The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.
restaurant.note: Male and female are separate cells here, both 1 per 75. Florida's potty-parity rule (Section 403.1.3) can raise the women's count above the table once the men's side has more than two fixtures. Bars and nightclubs are a different row (1 per 40).

school.urinals: No urinal column; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 67 percent of the required water closets in educational occupancies.
school.lavatories: 1 per 50 (one cell spanning male and female)
school.quote: 3 | Educational | Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink
school.note: One row for all educational facilities: the table does not separate elementary from secondary schools. Public schools and Florida colleges also fall under Section 453 of the Building volume (State Requirements for Educational Facilities), which adds layout rules (toilets on each floor, within 200 feet) and refers back to the code for ratios.

sex_split.text: Halve the occupant load: half male, half female, unless approved statistics show another split. A multi-user room for all genders is counted on the whole occupant load.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half.
sex_split.exception_quote: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Any fraction rounds up to the next whole fixture. In a building with several occupancies, add the fractions first, then round up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.
rounding.footnote_a_quote: The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are never required by the table. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies and up to 50 percent in all others. Each urinal needs its own screens (Section 405.3.5).
urinal_substitution.quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
urinal_substitution.urinal_partition_quote: Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required at 15 or fewer total occupants (any use), 25 or fewer in a business occupancy, or 100 or fewer in a mercantile occupancy. Where each sex needs only one water closet, two family or assisted-use rooms may serve instead.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.
small_occupancy_exception.family_rooms_quote: Where a building or tenant space requires a separate toilet facility for each sex and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted to serve as the required separate facilities.

occupant_load.text: The occupant load comes from the Building volume: Table 1004.5 gives floor area per occupant (business areas 150 gross sq ft; assembly with tables and chairs 15 net sq ft; classrooms 20 net sq ft; shops and vocational rooms 50 net sq ft); fixed seats are counted by seat.
occupant_load.quote: The number of occupants shall be computed at the rate of one occupant per unit of area as prescribed in Table 1004.5.
table_quotes: Shops and other vocational room areas | 50 net
occupant_load.pointer_quote: The number of occupants shall be determined by the Florida Building Code, Building.

worked_examples.how: 50 / 2 = 25 per sex. Water closets, 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50: 25 / 25 = 1, rounded up = 1. Lavatories, 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80: 25 / 40 = 0.625, rounded up = 1. Urinals: none required by the table; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 50 percent of the men's water closets: 50% of 1 = 0.5, so at most 0 (read here as rounding down, since the rule is 'not more than').

100 / 2 = 50 per sex. Water closets, 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50: 50 / 25 = 2, rounded up = 2. Lavatories, 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80: 50 / 40 = 1.25, rounded up = 2. Urinals: none required by the table; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 50 percent of the men's water closets: 50% of 2 = 1, so at most 1 (read here as rounding down, since the rule is 'not more than').

200 / 2 = 100 per sex. Water closets, 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50: first 50 = 2, remainder 50 / 50 = 1, rounded up = 1, total 3. Lavatories, 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80: first 80 = 2, remainder 20 / 80 = 0.25, rounded up = 1, total 3. Urinals: none required by the table; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 50 percent of the men's water closets: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so at most 1 (read here as rounding down, since the rule is 'not more than').

Lavatories, 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80: first 80 = 2, remainder 120 / 80 = 1.5, rounded up = 2, total 4. Urinals: none required by the table; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace up to 50 percent of the men's water closets: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so at most 2 (read here as rounding down, since the rule is 'not more than').

confidence_reason: The 8th Edition table and rules were read in full, but on UpCodes, not on the official ICC viewer (captcha / HTTP 403). The same three ratios appear in the Florida Building Commission's own supplement document for the 9th Edition, which is an official source.

ninth_edition_2026.summary: The published 9th Edition (2026) text was not read (not on UpCodes on 2026-11-24; the ICC viewer blocks automated access). Two official Florida Building Commission documents were read instead. Neither shows a change to the ratios in the Restaurant, Business or Educational rows.

analysis_of_changes.table_403_1_quote: Minimum plumbing fixtures have been added for the following: Ambulatory care facilities and outpatient clinics as a new description applicable to the Business classification.
analysis_of_changes.section_424_2_quote: This section has been revised to clarify that the substitutions permitted are for males according to Table 403.1.
analysis_of_changes.section_403_1_2_quote: New language has been added requiring the number of fixtures in single-user toilets, single-user bathing fixtures and family or assisted-use toilets to be deducted proportionately from the required gender ratios of Table 403.1.
analysis_of_changes.note: The analysis lists every change to Table 403.1 (new ambulatory care and care-facility rows, hospitals and nursing homes split, correctional rows split, hotel and apartment wording); it names no change to the Restaurant or Educational rows or to the Business office ratio. 'Section deleted' refers to 8th Edition 403.2.1, two family or assisted-use rooms serving as the separate facilities.

building_analysis.quote: The table has been revised for consistency with changes to Table 403.1 in the 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code, Plumbing.
building_analysis.table_1004_5_quote: Information technology equipment facilities have been added to the table with an occupant load factor of 500 gross.

supplement.note: 'Supplement to the 8th Edition (2023) FBC, Plumbing', a code-development document for the 9th Edition. It is a Word file whose struck-out and added text could not be told apart once converted to plain text, and it is not the final published code. The Business description there reads 'non-medical professional services' and drops 'ambulatory care', matching the analysis. Cells are joined here with ' | '; in the file each ratio is split across several lines.

to_confirm: 9th Edition (2026), effective 2026-12-31: the published Table 403.1 / Table 2902.1 was not read. The Florida Building Commission's Analysis of Changes and its supplement show the same ratios for the three rows (restaurants 1 per 75, lavatories 1 per 200; business 1 per 25 for the first 50 then 1 per 50, lavatories 1 per 40 for the first 80 then 1 per 80; educational 1 per 50, lavatories 1 per 50). Open the published 9th Edition in a browser (codes.iccsafe.org) and confirm the three rows before 2026-12-31.

9th Edition differences that do affect the page, per the Analysis of Changes: ambulatory care and outpatient clinics leave the general Business row for a row of their own; Section 424.2 says urinals substitute for the men's water closets; fixtures in single-user and family rooms are deducted proportionately from each sex's count (403.1.2); the section letting two family or assisted-use rooms stand in for separate men's and women's rooms (8th Edition 403.2.1) is deleted; urinal privacy rules move to Section 405.3.5 (Plumbing) / 2903.1.5 (Building).

Whether Florida's potty-parity section (403.1.3) and Sections 403.1.4 and 403.2.2 carry into the 9th Edition unchanged: the Analysis of Changes lists no change to them, but the published text was not read. In the supplement the 'Restrooms and changing facilities respective to sex' heading appears as 403.2.1, so the number may change.
Read the 8th Edition table once on the official ICC viewer in a browser (codes.iccsafe.org/content/FLPC2023P1, Chapter 4) to lift this entry from medium to high; it was read on UpCodes only.

Potty parity for restaurants: the section does not say how a 3:2 result with a fraction rounds (3 men's fixtures x 1.5 = 4.5), and whether a given restaurant falls under the Chapter 509 exception depends on its licence and banquet rooms. Section 553.86, Florida Statutes, was not read. Confirm with the City of Miami Building Department before publishing a women's count above the table figure.
Urinal substitution: the code says 'not more than' 67 or 50 percent; the worked examples round the allowed number of urinals down. Confirm with the Building Department if the page states a maximum.

Public K-12 schools: Section 453 of the Building volume (State Requirements for Educational Facilities) and Florida Department of Education rules may set student toilet ratios beyond Table 403.1; Section 453.16.1 only says 'in ratios ... as required by the Florida Building Code, Florida law, and federal requirements'. Private schools use the table row as read.

No City of Miami or Miami-Dade County amendment to the fixture table was found, but the Miami-Dade County Code (Chapter 8) was not read; the city page mentions 'codes and regulations established by the State of Florida and Miami-Dade County'.
The Restaurant and Educational rows of the Building volume's Table 2902.1 were compared with Table 403.1 as text only (cell spans checked for the Business row).
